questions.q: The area of the region bounded by the curve $y^2=x^3$, the y-axis and the lines $y=1$ and $y=8$ is
The area enclosed by the curve $x=\sqrt3\cos\theta, y=\sqrt3\sin\theta$ is
questions.explanation: This is a circle of radius $\sqrt3$, so its area is $\pi(\sqrt3)^2=3\pi$ sq. units.

questions.q: The area bounded by the curve $y=\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)$, x axis, the lines x = 0 and $x=3\pi$ is
The area of the region bounded by the curve $y=x^2$ and the line $y=16$ is
The area of the region bounded by the line $y = x + 1$, and the lines $x = -3$, $x = 3$ and the x-axis is
In the interval $(0, \pi/2)$, area lying between the curves $y = \tan x$ and $y = \cot x$ and the X-axis is
questions.explanation: The curves meet at $x=\pi/4$; area $=\int_0^{\pi/4}\tan x\,dx+\int_{\pi/4}^{\pi/2}\cot x\,dx = \dfrac12\ln2+\dfrac12\ln2=\ln2$.

questions.q: Area of the region bounded by the curve y = tan x, the x-axis and the line x = $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ is
The area of the region bounded by y = $\sqrt{16-x^2}$ and x $-$ axis is
questions.explanation: This curve is the upper half of a circle of radius 4, so the correctly bounded area is $8\pi$ sq units, which is not among the printed options; KEA awarded grace marks for this defective question (closest listed option taken here is 16$\pi$).

questions.q: The area of the region bounded by the curve $y^2=8x$ and the line $y=2x$ is
The area of the region bounded by the line $y=2x+1$, x-axis and the ordinates $x=-1$ and $x=1$ is
questions.explanation: The line crosses the x-axis at $x=-1/2$; summing the absolute areas on $[-1,-1/2]$ and $[-1/2,1]$ gives $1/4+9/4=5/2$.

questions.q: The area of the region above X-axis included between the parabola $y^2=x$ and the circle $x^2+y^2=2x$ in square units is
questions.explanation: For $0\le x\le1$ the circle lies above the parabola; the area between them is $\int_0^1\sqrt{1-(x-1)^2}\,dx-\int_0^1\sqrt x\,dx=\dfrac{\pi}{4}-\dfrac{2}{3}$.

questions.q: The area of the region bounded by Y-axis, $y=\cos x$ and $y=\sin x;\ 0\le x\le \dfrac{\pi}{2}$ is
questions.explanation: The curves meet at $x=\pi/4$; the area is $\int_0^{\pi/4}(\cos x-\sin x)\,dx=[\sin x+\cos x]_0^{\pi/4}=\sqrt2-1$.

questions.q: The area of the region bounded by the curve $y=\cos x$ between $x=0$ and $x=\pi$ is
The area bounded by the line $y=x$, x-axis and ordinates $x=-1$ and $x=2$ is
The area of the region bounded by the curve $y=x^2$ and the line $y=16$ is
Area of the region bounded by the curve $y=\cos x$, $x=0$ and $x=\pi$ is
Area lying between the curves $y^2 = 2x$ and $y = x$ is
questions.explanation: The curves meet at $x=0,2$; Area $=\int_0^2(\sqrt{2x}-x)\,dx=\dfrac{2}{3}$ sq. units.

questions.q: Area bounded by $y = x^3$, $y = 8$ and $x = 0$ is ____
The area of the region bounded by the lines y = mx, x = 1, x = 2, and x axis is 6 sq. units, then 'm' is
Area of the region bounded by two parabolas y = $x^2$ and x = $y^2$ is
The area bounded by the curve $y=\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)$, x-axis and lines $x=0$ and $x=3\pi$ is
questions.explanation: Over $[0,3\pi]$, $x/3$ ranges over $[0,\pi]$ where sine is non-negative, so area $=\int_0^{3\pi}\sin(x/3)\,dx=6$.

questions.q: If the area between $y=mx^2$ and $x=my^2$ ($m>0$) is $\dfrac14$ sq. units, then value of $m$ is ............
questions.explanation: The area between the curves is $\displaystyle\int_0^{1/m}\left[\sqrt{x/m}-mx^2\right]dx=\dfrac{1}{3m^2}$. Setting this to $\dfrac14$ gives $m=\dfrac{2}{\sqrt3}$, which does not exactly match any given option; KEA awarded a grace mark for this question.

questions.q: The area bounded by the curve $y=\begin{cases}x^2, & x<0\\ x, & x\ge0\end{cases}$ and the line $y=4$ is
The area bounded between the parabola $y^2=4x$ and the line $y=2x-4$ is equal to
questions.explanation: The curves meet at $y=-2,4$. Integrating w.r.t. $y$: $\int_{-2}^{4}\left[\dfrac{y+4}{2}-\dfrac{y^2}{4}\right]dy = 9$ sq. units.
